text: My husband and I got eloped here. Everyone was so nice and friendly. Our photographer was running late and city clerk told us they’d try their best to wait. Our justice of peace, Paula, is a gem! I’m so thankful for her empathy, consideration and warmth. It was so stressful but her humanity made everything so much better! We were able to take photos throughout the space and no one gave us a hard time. We had an amazing elopement here!

I wish I could give this an honest review of a 4 or a 5, because I know that the people who put it there were trying to solve a universal problem and had a kind heart. However, it must be noted that maintenence was a huge issue. It was completely covered in graffiti. It was completely unclean, with tissues all over the place. Lights in the small box were years away- it was completely dark. Although the flush was operative, the hand washing station was not. It was seeming that nobody had the responsibility of cleaning this place, as it was clear that it had not been cleaned in days, if not weeks.
If possible, steer clear of their restroom, and find a local shop.

Great park for such a hidden location. When I go here, there's usually only 2 other people, and it's a nice little place to hang out, with picnic benches. I wouldn't go here if your looking for walk. They should install bathrooms, or at least an outhouse. Definently a good park with not much litter. Suitable for all ages.

Harvard Square never disappoints! I recently took my aunt for a visit, and we had such a lovely time soaking in the atmosphere. One of our favorite stops was the The Harvard Coop—and of course, we couldn’t leave without picking up some merchandise!

What made this visit extra special was how surprisingly uncrowded it was. We were able to stroll comfortably, browse at our own pace, and truly enjoy the charm of the Square without the usual hustle and bustle.

It’s always such a classic Boston experience—great shopping, beautiful surroundings, and that unmistakable Harvard vibe. A must-visit every time!

We went to celebrate a friends 30th birthday, it was my first time here! 1/2 of the space was empty to become a dance floor later in the night. They had a fun cocktail menu. I mostly stuck to bottled beer but the cocktails and mocktails that my friends had they said were delicious.

The three exhibits on display were quite underwhelming… I highly recommend spending more time looking around the MIT buildings and public works of art on display that are scattered throughout the campus.

AKA 'Acorns'. The basketball courts are smooth with nice concrete ledges surrounding them.

It is hard to get the sound of the Memorial Drive cars out of your head as they are only a few yards from this park with no real barriers blocking the sound.

This museum is fun for all ages. From the amazing rocks and geodes to the life sized animals and dinosaur fossils,  it's  just a good time and a great way to spend a couple of hours. I really loved the Americas exhibit. Compared to other museums,  it's not as pricey. And the commute to get to the museum is fairly simple and doesn't take that long

This station is epic and famous, but not the cleanest.
We really enjoyed though visiting Harvard and passing through here seemed like being part of a movie.
We needed to use the bathroom and it was closed. So not great. To be noted that this is a place this Harvard square where it is really difficult to find a toilet.

Lovely sitting under the fairy lights in a comfy Adirondack chair, while a busker played songs from the 70s.  I was right next to, and under, the giant tree.  I’d like to know the age of that tree if anyone knows.
